The Simister Island junction of the M60 Manchester Outer Ring Road will be closed - and the motorway shut in both directions to junction 17 (Whitefield) - on the weekends of 26 September and 10 October, National Highways said. title: Frustration over months of sinkhole repairs on Alan Turing Way

input.lead: Part of Alan Turing Way in east Manchester has been closed since March with no signs of it reopening
input.summary: Part of Alan Turing Way in east Manchester has been closed since March with no signs of it reopening
input.evidence_text: Frustration over months of sinkhole repairs on Alan Turing Way - BBC News Image source, Manchester Evening News/LDRS Image caption, Manchester City Council is conducting investigative works on the sinkhole By George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago A sinkhole has halted traffic in a busy area of Manchester causing months of frustration for residents and commuters. Part of Alan Turing Way in east Manchester was closed in March and there are no signs of it reopening any time soon. The northbound section of the road between Ashton Old Road and Grey Mare Lane has been coned off with Manchester City Council conducting investigative works that are yet to be completed. Newton Heath resident David Carey said he tries to avoid using the route during rush hours and even when he uses it in off-peak hours to visit family, a 20-minute journey takes more than an hour. The council said it was taking time to ensure public safety and called for patience. It is expected the work to fix the sinkhole would take a considerable amount of time, given its size, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) said. Carey said the traffic lights to get towards the junction where you can get to the diversions causes a large tailback. The 59-year-old Manchester City supporter said with the football season restarting, traffic around the Etihad Stadium will become unbearable at weekends, as well as weekdays. He added: "It's getting darker and we are diverting traffic to get around this. The potential for a road traffic accident increases significantly." He told the LDRS: "I appreciate the reason for the closure as it was a big sinkhole. But we are now more than 165 days, and counting, and we have not even got the completion of the study. No one knows how long it will take.

title: Trophy disappears during black pudding throwing contest

input.lead: Organisers are appealing for the trophy to be returned "with no questions asked"
input.summary: Organisers are appealing for the trophy to be returned "with no questions asked"
input.evidence_text: Trophy disappears during black pudding throwing contest - BBC News Image source, PHIL TAYLOR Image caption, The Black Pudding Throwing Championships trophy was named after organiser Phil Taylor who died last year By Rebecca Brahde Published 1 hour ago Celebrations for the official Black Pudding Throwing Championships were "subdued" after the trophy went missing during the event, organisers have said. June Weir, 73, from Wilpshire, Lancashire, won the annual event at The Oak pub in Ramsbottom, Bury, on Sunday, becoming the first female champion in its 100-year history. Organiser Paul Jenkins said the presentation "lacked its sparkle" after the trophy disappeared from the prize table between 11:40 and 13:30 BST. Now, he is appealing for whoever took it to return it, "with no questions asked." Image source, PHIL TAYLOR Image caption, June Weir became the first female winner in the event's history Jenkins said although the plastic cup was not worth a lot in monetary value, its disappearance had "hit a nerve" with the community as it was named after Phil Taylor - a long-time organiser of the competition who died last year aged 73. The quirky sporting event, which has been running for more than a century and raises money for charity, sees throwers hurl black puddings at yorkshire puddings. Although Jenkins described this year's competition as the best event to date – with record crowds and Weir becoming the first female in its history becoming a joint winner – celebrations were "slightly subdued" when the presentation party realised the trophy had gone missing, he said. title: Manchester teens remain in custody over counter-terror probe

input.lead: The 19-year-olds were arrested in a Jewish neighbourhood of Salford in the early hours of 6 September
input.summary: The 19-year-olds were arrested in a Jewish neighbourhood of Salford in the early hours of 6 September
input.evidence_text: Manchester teens remain in custody over counter-terror probe - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The pair were remanded in custody to appear back at the same court on 21 September Published 14 September 2026 Two teenagers have appeared in court after police launched a counter-terror investigation. Harley Elliot and McKenzie Smyth, both aged 19, appeared in the dock at Manchester Magistrates' Court for a brief hearing where both were remanded into custody for a further seven days. Both are charged with possession of offensive weapons in a public place, a hammer and a kitchen knife, and having an article with intent to damage or destroy property, detailed in the charge sheet as spray paint and lighter fuel. Both men were arrested in a Jewish neighbourhood of Salford in the early hours of 6 September after police received reports of two men acting suspiciously. Police later said the investigation was being dealt with by counter-terror police. Elliot, of St Brelades Drive, Salford, and Smyth, of Grantham Drive, Bury, were later charged and remanded in custody. No pleas were entered and there were no applications for bail. The court was told a police investigation was "ongoing". Chair of the bench Ronnie Marshall remanded both men into custody to appear back at the same court on 21 September. title: Calls for public inquiry into Manchester synagogue terror attack

input.lead: The chief coroner says sensitive MI5 evidence means inquests may not be suitable
input.summary: The chief coroner says sensitive MI5 evidence means inquests may not be suitable
input.evidence_text: The chief coroner overseeing inquests into the deaths of two men killed in the attack on a Manchester synagogue is to ask the government to hold a public inquiry instead Judge Alexia Durran, chief coroner of England and Wales, said she would write to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to recommend the inquests be converted into a public inquiry after being told some MI5 material could not be heard in open court because of national security concerns Inquests were planned into the deaths of Adrian Daulby, 53, and Melvin Cravitz, 66, following the attack by Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, a Syrian-born British citizen, on Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue in Manchester last October Inquests have no mechanism to hold secret or private hearings, excluding press and public To carry out a full investigation, involving hearing sensitive material in private, would require a public inquiry, which can hold some of the hearings behind closed doors with press and public excluded Judge Durran made the decision to ask for a public inquiry be established following the pre-inquest hearing on 4 September

title: Greater Manchester Mayor eyes 2050 underground trains opening date

input.lead: Bev Craig says the city region needs to plan for the future and this means going underground
input.summary: Bev Craig says the city region needs to plan for the future and this means going underground
input.evidence_text: Plans to create Greater Manchester's own London Underground-style transport system have been backed by mayor Bev Craig, with 2050 eyed as a potential opening date The scheme could cost tens of billions and take decades to build - with the need for government backing - but has been described by Craig as the "only option" for the county's future Transport for Greater Manchester's (TfGM) timeline for the project could see detailed plans and a business case ready by 2030, with a push to start building by around 2040 and a 2050 opening date Craig said: "In Greater Manchester we've started planning for what future is possible, and that means going underground." The idea was separate from demands from city leaders in Manchester for an underground railway station at Manchester Piccadilly, which would play a part in boosting railway travel supporting the £45bn Northern Powerhouse Rail project But a new underground station at Piccadilly is seen as an essential "first step" ahead of wider plans for Greater Manchester, including the potential for a future underground tube network

title: Andy Burnham cancels engagements after death of father

input.lead: Burnham has previously said his father did not know he had become prime minister due to his Alzheimer's
input.summary: Burnham has previously said his father did not know he had become prime minister due to his Alzheimer's
input.evidence_text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has cancelled official engagements on Monday and Tuesday following the death of his father Roy, who had Alzheimer's He had been due to host a meeting of business leaders in Downing Street on Monday, and was expected to speak at the annual trade union TUC Congress in Brighton on Tuesday In July, Burnham spoke about his father's condition and said it had influenced his drive to reform adult social care in England He had also said his father's illness was so advanced that he did not know his son had become prime minister Burnham told the BBC that while his father could not be there when he entered No 10 to take up the role, he and his mother had "exchanged a few words about my dad and how proud he would be" "That's a little hard, but then again I've said, it's their achievement", he told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg in July

input.evidence_text: Homelessness Rough sleeping rises in Greater Manchester as Andy Burnham pledges to end crisis by Christmas The number of rough sleepers across Greater Manchester went up in June, new figures show, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham vows to get every rough Comments News Paul Gallagher 05:57, 14 Sep 2026 The number of people sleeping rough across Greater Manchester has reached one of its highest levels in six years, according to new data released as former mayor Andy Burnham pledged to make homelessness a national priority Government data shows there were 444 rough sleepers across the ten boroughs of Greater Manchester in June 2026, up from 402 in June 2025 - a rise of 42 people, or 10.4 per cent. It is the highest figure for June, and the fourth highest monthly total since October 2020 The figures land as Mr Burnham - who made ending rough sleeping his first pledge on entering Downing Street in July - is pushing ahead with a national drive to get every rough sleeper off the streets by Christmas , backed by a £442 million funding package The biggest driver of the rise in Greater Manchester was Manchester city itself, where the number of rough sleepers in June jumped from 149 last summer to 195 - an increase of 46 people Tameside saw the second sharpest rise, climbing from 21 to 33, while Trafford rose from 6 to 10 and Bury edged up from 29 to 31. Not all boroughs saw increases. Salford , Oldham , Rochdale and Bolton recorded slightly lower numbers sleeping rough on their streets

title: Expanding ‘trainer flat' scheme helps care leavers to thrive in adulthood - Rochdale Borough Council

input.lead: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council
input.summary: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council
input.evidence_text: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council Living alone for the first time can be a daunting experience, but it can be an even greater challenge for those who have grown up in care as some may only have a limited support network that they can rely on This can make adjusting to new responsibilities such as paying utility bills, managing a tenancy agreement, budgeting and keeping on top of household chores harder However, through the help of the local authority’s trainer flat scheme, of which there are now 14 across the borough, cared for young people aged 17 and over are being offered the perfect stepping stone to safely prepare for life on their own Fully furnished and equipped with everyday household goods, these flats provide young people with the time and support they need to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to successfully transition into adulthood This support is offered without the financial pressures normally associated with setting up a home, with the young people not required to contribute towards gas, electricity, water and other property-related utility costs until they turn 18

input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
